causes.quote: Wind output was lower than forecast, averaging 163 MW out of around 2,763 MW of installed capacity during the high prices. This equates to around 6% of installed capacity in South Australia.

causes.label: network_outage
causes.quote: A planned outage of the Heywood to South East line meant flows into South Australia on the Heywood interconnector were reduced to 50 MW due to FCAS requirements. This meant that South Australia was unable to import sufficient low-priced capacity during the high prices.

causes.label: network_outage
causes.quote: There was a planned outage of the Heywood to South East line, originally scheduled to end at 5.30 pm on 28 July. However, at 11.42 am it was extended to 29 July. The outage meant flows on Heywood were reduced to 50 MW due to FCAS requirements and South Australia was unable to import sufficient low-priced capacity during the high prices. Murraylink flows were also reduced due to system normal constraints in place to prevent voltage collapse.

During the morning high price periods, average wind output for all regions (including Queensland) was 954 MW out of around 13,689 MW of installed capacity. This equates to around 7% of installed capacity in the NEM. causes.label: unscheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: Baseload outages meant that 920 MW of generally low-priced capacity was unavailable in Victoria on 5 August. EnergyAustralia's Yallourn unit 1 (which has a 360 MW baseload capacity) had been offline since 2 August due to an unplanned outage. At 5.00 pm, EnergyAustralia's Loy Yang A unit 4 went offline due to an unplanned unit outage removing 560 MW of available baseload capacity.

Flows over the Murraylink interconnector was also limited to 22 MW due to planned network outage on the Kerang to Wemen line.

peak_price.quote: The price reached $5,623 per MWh at 8 am.

rebid_set_price.quote: Rebidding for commercial and technical reasons contributed to the high price (Appendix G).

causes.label: wind_output
causes.quote: Wind output averaged 602 MW out of around 2,763 MW installed capacity during the high prices, which equates to around 22% of installed capacity in South Australia.

causes.label: solar_output
causes.quote: Average solar output was 191 MW out of around 600 MW of maximum capacity due to cloudy conditions. The cloudy conditions also meant rooftop solar output was low which resulted in higher demand.

causes.label: demand
causes.quote: Total demand at 10 am was 1,425 MW compared to the previous month average of 1,073 MW.

causes.label: network_outage
causes.quote: system normal constraints on the Heywood interconnector capped wind, solar and battery generation in the south-east region. Murraylink was also on a planned outage with flows reduced to 0 MW which limited South Australia's ability to access cheaper generation to alleviate the high prices.

causes.label: scheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: Engie's Pelican Point station (478 MW registered capacity) had been on a planned outage since 31 August

causes.label: ramp_rates
causes.quote: Dry Creek unit 2 could not start fast enough to help lower the price. The Dry Creek unit had 35 MW priced at the floor (-$1,000 per MWh) for the 10 am 5-minute interval, none of which could be dispatched in time.

causes.label: rebids
causes.quote: Rebidding for commercial reasons contributed to the high price (Appendix H).

causes.label: network_outage
causes.quote: Equipment maintenance led to a planned line outage on the Para to Parafield Gardens West 275 kV line. This resulted in three stations (Snapper Point, Pelican Point and Bolivar) that had 267 MW of low-priced capacity constrained, preventing low-priced capacity making it to market. ... Flows on Murraylink into South Australia was reduced to around 25 MW out of its 220 MW nominal capacity due to a planned line outage around the Balranald area in New South Wales to avoid voltage collapse.
